text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 12.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: C041a — Supermodes of the strip-waveguide directional coupler (Sec 4.1.6, Fig 4.13, p.105)

text.style: font-size: 9.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Two 500 × 220 nm strip cores, solved as one coupled pair: in-phase lobes — symmetric, out-of-phase — antisymmetric.

text.style: font-size: 7px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: asymmetry is a normalisation artefact, not physics

text.style: font-size: 7.5px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #a1a1a6

g.text: Fig 4.13 twin maps are synthetic schematics reproducing the sign signatures (bridge vs null); no gap value, wavelength, or neff is stated for the strip coupler.

text.style: font-weight: 700; font-size: 9px; font-family: 'Inter', 'DejaVu Sans'; text-anchor: start; fill: #f6f6f6

g.text: Takeaway: symmetric = same-sign lobes bridged across the gap; antisymmetric = opposite signs with a centre null — strip couples more weakly than rib.
